# Stories: implement, or push back

For the AI asked to work on stories (the person can simply say "do the stories"). A story is one
plain-text file in **stories/new/**, written in plain English by a person: a BA, a tester, a product
owner. Work through every file there (README.md aside), one at a time, and for each: **implement it, or push back**.
Never guess to make a story fit. And never change the suite's rules to make a story's test pass
(AI-README.md, "Off limits"): a story its test can't pass the rules with is a story to push back.

## 1. Read it

- **Its id** is the first word shaped like `INJ-592` (letters, a dash, digits), as written: in the
  file name ("inj-592 contact form.txt" has the id `inj-592`), else in the story's text above any `----`
  line. Neither: the file name, without its extension. SuiteRulesTest reads it the same way.
- **Its title** is its first line, the id left out, when that line names the story; when it is already
  a step ("Start on the home page..."), the file name's words, the id left out.
- **Its steps and outcomes** are the rest. Steps like "scroll down" need no code: a click scrolls to
  what it clicks, and a check looks at the whole page.
- Some text may already follow a `---- PUSHBACK ...` line: an earlier pass sent it back, and the person
  has edited the story since. Read all of it and decide afresh.

## 2. Check it against what this suite knows

Everything a story names must match exactly one thing here:

| A story names | Look in |
| --- | --- |
| a page ("the contact page", "Careers") | GLOSSARY.md, then the page classes' Javadoc |
| a link or menu item ("Services > Cloud") | GLOSSARY.md (header, footer and page links, with the method that follows each) |
| a button, field, dropdown, checkbox | controls/<PageClass>.md, controls/Everywhere.md |
| text on a page, a heading | the page class's Elements and Javadoc; crawl/ for what the crawl read |
| anything on a crawled page, with or without a locator | crawl/pages/<path>.html: the page's HTML as the crawl saw it (data-sb-hidden="true" marks what a visitor could not see then) |
| a page or state the crawl never saw | saved-pages/<PageClass>/ (see saved-pages/README.md) |
| test data, a login | SiteConfig values and secrets, and the team rules below |

**Check every locator a story gives you** against the page it is on, as the crawl saw it: a locator
that looks right can find nothing, or several things. Where Suite Builder is installed:

```
suite locate xoveconsulting-com-tests <page> "<locator>"
```

(`<page>` is its path, like `/careers`.) Exactly one element: use it. None, or several: push back, saying
what it found. Otherwise read crawl/pages/<path>.html and search it. A page the crawl never read has
no snapshot: use the story's locator only if it gives one, and write "unverified: <why>" in the
IMPLEMENTED note; with none, push back and ask for a saved page. An element the story names without a
locator: find it in the page's snapshot, and check the locator you write the same way.

## 3. Push back when

- **Its locator is wrong.** A locator the story gives finds nothing, or several things, on the page as
  crawled. Quote what it found (suite locate lists it), and ask for one that finds exactly one.
- **It is vague.** A word matches nothing here, or more than one thing ("Contact Us": the header link or
  the footer form?). Name the words and the candidates.
- **The crawl could not have seen it.** It happens after a click, behind a login, or after a form is
  sent, and no saved page shows it. Ask for exactly that page: which page, saved when (after doing what).
- **It has nothing to check.** No outcome a visitor would see ("the user uses the form"). Ask what should
  be true afterwards.
- **It checks more than one thing.** A story has one outcome, checked once, at the end. Two outcomes
  ("the heading says Careers, then the job section shows") are two stories: suggest the split, one
  line each. Arriving on a page needs no check of its own: every page checks it has loaded.
- **It is unsafe on the live site.** It sends a form, orders, pays, signs up, deletes, or emails someone,
  and the team rules below don't point the suite at a test copy of the site (`-DbaseUrl`). Ask for one,
  or for the team's permission in the rules.
- **It needs data the suite does not have.** A login, an order number: ask for the SiteConfig names.

To push back, **append** to the story file (never change the person's text) and leave it in stories/new/:

```
---- PUSHBACK (2026-09-28) ----
Not implemented: <one sentence: why>.
Needed:
- <exactly what would make it implementable, one line each>
```

## 4. Implement it

Follow AI-README.md, "From a story to a test": elements (from controls/ when listed there), actions and
checks in the page classes' YOURS blocks, and one story class in `src/test/java/com/xoveconsulting/tests/cases/`
(ai/recipes/write-a-story-test.md):

- **Named after the id**: letters and digits kept, the first upper case: `engi-101` is `Engi101`.
- `@Story(value = "<id>", title = "<title>")` on the class, the id exactly as the story writes it.
- **One `@Test`**, its `@DisplayName` the title: the story as one chain of page methods, from the
  page it starts on to its **one** `verify()` at the end.
- Nothing after the `verify()`, no assertions, locators or Playwright calls in the story; the rules
  are in SUITE-RULES.md, and SuiteRulesTest checks every one.
- Run it if you can: `mvn test -Dtest=<StoryClass>,SuiteRulesTest`. If you cannot, check every call you wrote
  against ai/API.md (the rules cannot see a call that won't compile), say it was not compiled, and give the person that line. A failure the site causes goes in KNOWN-ISSUES.md; a failure you caused, you fix.

Then **move the file to stories/done/** and append:

```
---- IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-28) ----
Test: <StoryClass> (src/test/java/com/xoveconsulting/tests/cases/<StoryClass>.java)
Added: <elements, actions and checks, by name>
Run: <passed / not run here: the line to run>
```

SuiteRulesTest checks that every story in stories/done/ has a story test with its id.

## 5. Report

End with a short list for the person: each story's id and what happened ("inj-592: implemented as
Inj592, passed"; "inj-593: pushed back: which Contact Us?").

## Your team's rules

What your team wants on top of these (the tracker's id format, what may run against which site, who
may approve a story that sends a form). They win over the rules above.
